title: Linked List Cycle II
description:
Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If the list has no cycle, return None.

The input describes the list as {"values": [...], "pos": i}, where pos is the index of the node the last node points back to, or -1 when the list ends normally. pos is not passed to your function.

Because two nodes can hold the same value, your answer is reported as the index of the node you return within the original list, or -1 when you return None. Return the node itself — the index is worked out for you.

Constraints:

  • The list holds between 0 and 10^4 nodes.
  • -10^5 <= Node.val <= 10^5.
  • pos is -1 or a valid index in the list.
  • Aim for O(1) extra memory.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The tail links back to index 1, so the cycle starts at the second node.
The tail links back to the head, so the cycle starts at index 0.
No cycle, so there is no starting node.
